nodes.title: Belarusian identification as Litvins
nodes.subtitle: Analyzing the idea of "Litvin" being one of the endonym of Belarusians.

blocks.text: The reason this is extremely important is because "Litvin" is a slavic word that translates to Lithuanian. Meaning any historical document that mentions the exonym Lithuania/n would also refer to the Belarusians. This helps us create a higher level of evidence required from the opposing side: their documents must explicitly write "Lietuviai", which was an endonym used by non-slavic speakers of the GDL. It also helps us understand a lot of historical documents from another perspective, as we no longer categorize Belarusians as Ruthenians only.

nodes.title: Belarus: heir of Grand Duchy of Lithuania
nodes.subtitle: Full Litvinist breakdown of the history of Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Analyzing all arguments from both sides and using verified information. Non-biased perspective.

blocks.text:
What is litvinism? Litvinism is a historiographical perspective of the history of Grand Duchy of Lithuania. It establishes that the historical Grand Duchy of Lithuania closer aligns with the modern Belarusian state, rather than the modern Lithuania, which more aligns with the historical Samogitia.
Note: Both Belarus and Lithuania have claims to the state, with both nations using their versions of "Lithuania" as their personal endonyms.

blocks.label: Peter Von Koppen Studies 1860
blocks.text: Peter von Koppen is the most dedicated ethnographer of the Russian empire and conducted the highest quality studies of that era. In his studies He mentions that the ethnonym "Litvin" was especially widespread in Belarusian-speakers of Grodno, Vawkavysk, Slonim, Slutsk and Vileyka. He says the majority of priests used the phrase "lithuanians speaking belarusian".

blocks.label: MYKHAILO MAKSYMOVYCH 1839
blocks.text: Ukrainian historian writes in his book - *"Belarusian language or Lithuanian-Rusyn is referred to as "Lithuanian" and the speakers "Litvin" in the territory of Malorussia (Ukraine). That's why the west part of Chernigov governate whose speakers are Belarusian and descend from Radimovichs is called Lithuania"*

blocks.label: DICTIONARIES (1828+)
blocks.text:
In a Ukrainian dictionary by Hrinchenko from 1907, Litvin meant both Belarusian and Lithuanian. 
- Lithuania meant Lithuania and Belarusians.
- Litvinsky (Lithuanian) meant Belarusian.
These are sources from Hanna Barvinoks work, born 1828.
___
In a dictionary by Paval Bilecki (1839), it meant "title used by Ukrainians of Poltava to refer to the people  living on the other side of the Desna river.
___

blocks.label: HISTORICAL ANCEDOTES
blocks.text: In 1846, German historian Friedrich Kruse of the Dorpat University noted: "The true Lithuanians live in the former Voivodeships of Vilnius and Trakai, Novogrudok, Brest Litovsk, Minsk, Polotsk, Vitebsk, Mstislav and Smolensk"

items.note: Kruse, F. (1846). Ur-Geschichte des Esthnischen Volksstammes und der Kaiserlich-Russischen Ostseeprovinzen Liv-, Esth- und Curland überhaupt [Prehistory of the Estonian tribe and the Imperial Russian Baltic provinces...] (in German). Moskau. p. 128.

blocks.label: PETER VON KOPPEN STUDIES 1860
blocks.text:
On top of his observation, he also conducted many censuses on the self identification of European Russian empire, from the censuses we can see the identification of many cities:
- Lutsk: 620 belarusians, 2621 lithuanians (litvins)
- Radomyshyl: 452 belarusians, 32252 lithuanians (litvins)
- Novograd-Volynsk: 2381 belarusians, 1153 lithuanians (litvins)
- Ostroh: 1777 lithuanians, Ovruch: 5293 lithuanians
- Kyiv and Volyn Governates: 40233 belarusians, 49269 lithuanians (litvins)
--- 
- Brest district: 1205 belarusians, 7210 lithuanians (litvins)
- Pruzhany district: - belarusians, 27610 lithuanians (litvins)
- Kobryn district: 2614 belarusians, 22725 yatviags
- Grodno: 128640 lithuanians (litvins) and orthodox

blocks.label: ZAPORIZHIAN HOST RECORDS
blocks.text:
In the Cossack records, Litvin & Litvinenko were the most widespread surnames, with 155 records of it's usage.
___
Documents from the Cossack Hetmanate and the Chernihiv Consistory in 1735, 1761, and 1765 noted that the inhabitants of the Belarusian part of Severia "speak in the Lithuanian way" (Russian: говорятъ по литовску).

blocks.label: LITVINS OF THE SEVERIA
blocks.text:
In parts Chernigov, Smolensk, Starodub and nearby regions, the common identification was "Litvin". Those who identified as such were Belarusian-speaking, but referred to as Lithuanian-speaking back then.
___
1920 studies record 120k individuals potentially identified as Litvins in the Novozibovsk area.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Using these statistics, we can conclude litvin was an extremely widespread endonym, that reached into modern day northern Ukraine. Koppen's work comes from mid 19th century, which is over 50 years after the "belarusian" endonym was propagated by the Russian empire. Still, in spite of that, the litvin ethnonym remained and was majority in a lot of areas.

items.note: Тиханов, Н. Н. (1904). Брянский говор [Bryansk dialect]. Сборник отделения русского языка и словесности Императорской академии наук (in Russian). 76. СПб.: 119.

Lebedkin, c. 1860 (pp. 57–59): he counted 201,897 “Lithuanians” in Grodno governorate, 64.75% of them Orthodox. Merkys explains this by former Uniate clergy who “by old habit called themselves Lithuanians”.

nodes.title: Lithuania's and Belarus' old state endonyms
nodes.subtitle: Analyzing what Lithuanian's old endonym was: Litva, Aukstatija, Samogitia, Belarus, or all?

blocks.text:
This analysis relies on historical treaties and maps to determine which regions were considered which. The state's formal name was "The Grand Duchy of Lithuanian, Ruthenia and Samogitia.

The litvinist perspective views Belarus as Lithuania, Lithuania as Samogitia and Ruthenia as Ukraine. While the mainstream perspective treats Lithuania as Lithuania and Ruthenia as both Belarus and Ukraine.

blocks.label: Treaty of Melno/Konisberg 1400
blocks.text:
Also includes Treaty of Dubysa, Salynas, etc.
These treaties ceded Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights. The interesting part is that the treaties say: *"to cede Samogitia up to that Nevezis river"*.
When visualizing the treaty, it looks something like this:

blocks.caption: Over half of modern ethnic Lithuanian land ceded away

blocks.label: Nicolas de Fer 1700
blocks.text: Nicolas de Fer was a cartographer from France, who made a map of GDL on demand of the Swedish empire in the early 1700s.

blocks.caption: -# This is not the original, I made it easier to see as the original is using an archaic map style. It can be found easily on google with "Nicolas de Fer Lithuania"

steps.label: Explanation
steps.text:
A common argument from the opposing side is bringing up the 1420 Samogitian conference letters, in which under Vytautas name, several things are claimed:
- Samogitia is an integral part of GDL.
- Samogitians and Lithuanians speak the same language and are the same people
- Samogitia is the low land and Lithuania is the high land.
This argument essentially debunks the idea that the slavic people of Belarus couldve been Lithuanian

steps.label: Addition
steps.text:
There's no original of the letter, there's a print of it in latin by a Polish historian from the 19th century Tytus Dzialynski or from Antoni Puschachka. 
The main critique of the contents letter, is it's extremely out of place terminology and context:
- The letter makes extremely emotional and strong claims towards Samogitia, in spite of the fact Vytautas had previously given it up easily to the Teutonic Knights. 
- Later documents mentioning Samogitia and Lithuania as separated entities, like the states name. And other later documents mentioning Samogitia refuseing to subordinate to Lithuania or Rus.
- The letter uses terminology of "Aukstatija" and the "lowland/highland" which have never appeared in any document after this for over 300 years. 
- The letter makes an ethnic argument for the land, something that was extremely unpopular for the period it was written in.

steps.label: EXPLANATION
steps.text: A paper from the 16th century exists talking about the detailed composition of Grand Duchy of Lithuania. It writes "Lithuania consists of 4 core people: Samogitians, Lithuanians, Yotvingians and Semigallians, who all speak the Lithuanian language, but have some trouble understanding each other without practise.

steps.label: WHAT IT GETS RIGHT
steps.text: This paper does prove that the non-slavic (baltic) peoples of GDL, also used Lithuanian as their endonym.

steps.label: THE NUANCE
steps.text: This was a propaganda paper, dedicated to the era of Sarmatism. It mentions that these non-slavic (baltic) peoples of GDL are the real Romans/Italians, who were corrupted by evil Poles and Russians. He claims the state name was "Litalia" (Little Italy), but was corrupted by slavs to be Litva.

blocks.label: Treaty of Radnot 1656
blocks.text:
Following the treaty of Kiedenai, in which Lithuania accepts a union with Sweden, comes the Treaty of Radnot, which is a combination of many plans Sweden had for PLC. 
In the treaty, Sweden takes Samogitia, Kaunas, Livonia, Courland, parts of Dvina and Neris rivers, parts of Polock and Podlachia. It establishes an independent Cossack (Rus) state, and a Lithuanian state, both of which are in union with Sweden. 
This treaty, visualized below, helps us display what was considered Lithuania and what was Samogitia back then.

blocks.caption: -# The wikipedia page about the treaty of Kiedenai misinterprets the treaties content, in the treaty Sweden takes parts to itself and the rest it forms a union with, the person who wrote the page interpreted the parts it took for itself as the parts it formed a union with.

blocks.label: Treaty of Hadyach (Yuri Nemyrych) 1658
blocks.text: This is Yuri Nemyrychs version of the Treaty of Hadyach, he was an important role in the cossack history, this is considered the original version of the treaty, before cossacks had to make concessions to ratify it. This treaty being maximalist, shows us that the territories of the Rus correlate with the ethnic Ukrainian territories, which at that time identified as Rusyns. This allows us to infere that the lands past the drawn border did not identify as Rusyns, as otherwise they would be written down.

items.title: Acts of Visitation of Evangelical Reformers in 1669: Borders of White Rus' (BiaŁey Rusy

steps.label: Explanation
steps.text: This historical document mentions some modern Belarusian cities as part of White Ruthenia, which is used to claim that White Ruthenia is separate from Lithuania. However, it's a non sequitur. White ruthenia is used as a regional name in the document, like Black Ruthenia. For example: Galicia, Podollia, Bavaria. It also mentions these congregates were ruled in Kiedienai.

nodes.title: Ethnic Distribution
nodes.subtitle: Now, knowing the borders, we must analyze who actually lived in them, as lines alone dont tell us much.

blocks.label: Ethnic map of Duchy of Lithuania
blocks.text: Using the old borders of the Duchy of Lithuania and visualizing the ethnicities inside. This shows us how multi-ethnic the Lithuania proper region actually was, and how much of the Lithuania proper was Belarusian.

blocks.caption: What's interesting is the correlation of the Treaty of Radnots border and the ethnic distribution of Lithuanians.

blocks.label: Archeological Evidence
blocks.text:
Archeological research in many modern Lithuanian cities helps us reveal the ethnic distribution of them as far back as the 13th century:
- Vilnius: in around the 1270s, large waves of Ruthenians started arriving in the city, originating from the Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia (Rus). Founding the cities first settlements - Civitas Ruthenica.
- Kernave: following Vilnius, a wave of Ruthenians arrived in Kernave too, at around 1290s. 
- Trakai: it is unclear when exactly Ruthenians arrived in Trakai, but they were continuously mentioned through history and remained majority even up to the 19th century.

items.title: The settlements were actually Yotvingians, not Ruthenians.

steps.label: Explanation
steps.text: A common argument is that the burial site in Kernave was actually from Yotvingians and not Ruthenians.

steps.label: Vilnius
steps.text: This article provides an in depth analysis of the claims around Vilnius -> https://nashaniva.com/en/399220

steps.label: Kernave
steps.text: The burials in Kernave do contain some ornaments that represent the Baltic culture, while some contain clearly Slavic ornaments. It seems as unlike in Vilnius, the city had some Yotvingians who were in close relationship to the Ruthenians religiously. Claiming it was purely Yotvingian is unscientific, and illogical, considering the similiar dates of the bodies found.

blocks.text: This is a list crafted by Ruthenians of Novgorod, the content of which documents every orthodox settlement that had a Ruthenian delegation.

nodes.title: Addressing Counter-Arguments & Mainstream
nodes.subtitle: We will rely purely on the framework to debunk any arguments and the mainstream perspective.

blocks.text: Creating the framework of Litvinism.
Using the framework to address the mainstream historiographical perspective and potential counter arguemnts

blocks.label: Explanation
blocks.text: This argument uses the historical Union of Krewo to prove that Lithuania could not be a belarusian state, as belarusian slavs were Orthodox.

blocks.label: Rebuttal
blocks.text: This argument can be easily rebutted by the fact Danylo Romanovych (the ruler of Kingdom of Halych-Volhynia) planned to adopt Catholicism. This shows that a confirmed Ruthenian ruler from 1250s also used religion strategically.

blocks.label: Explanation
blocks.text: This argument claims the founding figures of the Lithuania state such as Mindaugas, Gediminas and others were of Baltic origin.

blocks.label: Clarifying "Baltic"
blocks.text: Firstly, "Baltic" is a modern exonym created in the 19th century, that did not exist during the time of GDL. What they mean by this argument is that the leading dynasty was non-slavic.

blocks.label: Ethnicity of the Elite
blocks.text:
To establish the ethnicity of the elite, we must know what endonym they used for themselves: litvin or lietuviai.

Currently, there are no documents showing the dynasty identifying as "lietuviai". Making the ethnicity of the dynasty unclear.

steps.label: Response
steps.text: The majority of modern-day Belarus was Baltic speaking until the slavs began moving further up, with languages like Dnipro-Baltic remaining up until the 13th century. This influenced the languages of the slavs moving there, especially so with the toponyms, hydronyms and personal names.

steps.label: Additionally
steps.text: It was quite widespread for east slavs to adopt names of different cultures, like variag nordic names.

steps.label: Rebuttal
steps.text: The leaders never had a concrete religion until the late 14th century. They were switching their religions diplomatically and strategically, sometimes practising paganism, then after a few years practising orthodoxy, then catholicism and repeating this cycle when convenient. This is evidenced by multiple chronicles (such as the Hypatian chronicle).

items.title: Gedimind was Baltic because of his N1c1 Haplogroup

steps.label: Explanation
steps.text: Genetic studies on Gediminds haplogroup lineage do show he has N1c1 DNA, this doesnt exactly mean he's non-slavic, however it does mean he comes from the area of around Vilnius (N-M231), meaning he was a local.

blocks.text: There's thousands of different arguments that can be made. I attempt to document any argument that requires additional detail that the framework doesn't cover, however any argument that is easily covered by our framework wont be mentioned. I'll explain how to refute them.

blocks.label: Identification
blocks.text:
Identify what type of argument it is, is it some historical document that supposedly refutes our perspective? Is it an attack to one of our core positions from our framework? Is it an attack on our logic?

A lot of arguments you will see go something like this - a document saying "An orthodox priest in Minsk from 1562 said he doesn't understand Lithuanian". In this case, you need to point out that Lithuanian could also refer to the Belarusian dialect, and the priest could've been Ruthenian (Ukrainian).  
Could also be something like "A church in Vilnius mentioning it supporting both Lithuanians and Ruthenians". In this case, Lithuanians here could also refer to Belarusians, while Ruthenians to Ukrainians.

Some arguments might attack our core premises, so you must use the sources I link to defend them.

blocks.label: NON-SLAVIC (BALTIC) INDIVIDUALS USING LITHUANIAN AS THEIR ENDONYM
blocks.text:
There's an abundance of documents and historical evidence to prove that the non-slavic baltic individuals of the GDL (that align with modern Lithuania) used a form of "Lithuanian" as their endonym too, that form being - "lietuviai".

The spread of it is unclear. We don't know whether the Samogitians also used it or had their own endonym.

blocks.label: EARLY LITHUANIA
blocks.text: The early usage of the term Lithuania does indeed refer to the non-slavic speakers of the modern Lithuania, as per the Polotsk records, which mention Polotsk recruiting Liv (Latvia) and Litva (lithuania

nodes.title: Rusyn-identifying individuals of the Carpthian Region should be considered a part of the Ukrainian ethnicity
nodes.subtitle: My framework covering the historical context, the logical framework of ethnicity, and the nuance of this topic. Analyzing arguments from both sides and making the strongest case.

blocks.text: Before getting into the details of the people themselves, we must first define the terms we are arguing. This is a TL;DR version of my existing logical framework on ethnicity.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: A group of people who share language, self-identification and have a shared historical trajectory
This thesis relies on my existing logical framework on ethnicity, which can be found in the environments tab.

blocks.label: AXIOMS AND ANALOGIES
blocks.text:
1) If a speech cannot be understood, it is not a dialect. 
2) If a speech can be somewhat understood, it has the potency to be categorized as a dialect.
3) If a speech is fully understandable and has minor differences, it has a potency to be categorized as a separate language.
___
For example, the Samogitian dialect of Lithuanian has a way lower mutual intelligibility than Ukrainian and Belarusian, yet one is considered a dialect and one a language.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: Political context is what drives the difference between language and dialect after a certain point of mutual intelligibility.
Showing the historical context of the endonym Rusyn.
Now that we established what an ethnicity is, we must analyze the 2 pillars: self identification and historical trajectory. Language versus dialect is drawn on the conclusion of those 2 pillars.

blocks.label: USAGE
blocks.text: Rusyn was an endonym of east slavs

blocks.label: PROBLEMS OF THE MAINSTREAM
blocks.text:
The mainstream definition - "An ethnicity is a group of humans who share language, culture, traditions, religion, history and have a common self identification"
___
1. Culture & Tradition: this is a baseless term that has no definition and shouldnt be used as a factor for ethnicities. Cultures are really region dependent and many ethnicities have tens or even hundreds of different cultures.
___
2. Religion: while religion can divide ethnicities it is not universal, for example with western Ukrainians following Catholicism while the rest Orthodoxy. 
___
3. History: I believe the history part needs to be expanded towards shared historical trajectory, to accommodate for intent and plans.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text:
Based on the critique, I rewrite the definition of ethnicity to be - 
=="A group of people who share language, self-identification and have a shared historical trajectory"==

blocks.label: AXIOMS
blocks.text:
1) If a speech cannot be understood, it is not a dialect. 
2) If a speech can be somewhat understood, it has the potency to be categorized as a dialect.
3) If a speech is fully understandable and has minor differences, it has a potency to be categorized as a separate language.
___
For example, the Samogitian dialect of Lithuanian has a way lower mutual intelligibility than Ukrainian and Belarusian, yet one is considered a dialect and one a language.

blocks.label: DIFFERENTIATION
blocks.text:
Axioms 2 and 3 show that these moments have the potency to be but not automatically are. 

The reasoning for this, is the only way to  decide whether a speech should be categorized a dialect or a language at this level of mutual intelligibility, is via a political examination.

blocks.label: CONCLUSION
blocks.text: Political context is what drives the difference between language and dialect after a certain point of mutual intelligibility.
